title: Sultanate of Kedah
capsule: The Sultanate of Kedah is among the oldest Islamic sultanates in Southeast Asia, traditionally dated to the conversion of its ruler King Phra Ong Mahawangsa as Sultan Mudzaffar Shah around 1136, on the northwestern Malay Peninsula where Gunung Jerai served as a navigational landmark for traders from India, Persia, and Arabia. British representative Francis Light obtained Penang Island in the 1780s under false promises of military protection against Siam, and Siam invaded and occupied Kedah in 1821, exiling the sultan for two decades until British mediation secured his restoration in 1842. The Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909 transferred Kedah to British protection as one of the Unfederated Malay States, formally ending Siamese suzerainty over the sultanate.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Kedah's core territory is well-documented from the 18th century onward in British and Siamese records; the extent of its earlier suzerainty over tributary polities and the exact inland frontier before European surveying are less precisely attested.
